title: gate_approves_spend counts a refusing answer worded Not approved, Do not spend, Never or Abort as approval, since only the first words no, refuse, decline, deny, reject and cancel are refusals
goal: bl_dispatch.gate_approves_spend treats an answer as a refusal when its first word is no, not, never, abort, refuse, decline, deny, reject, cancel or don (from don't), or its first two words are do not (a match on the answer's leading words, REFUSAL_WORDS extended and a two-word case added), so the paid-session stub stays for such an answer and an answer such as Approve or Yes still approves

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import bl_dispatch as d;g=lambda a:{"question":"Approve spend?","options":["yes",a],"answer":a};bad=[a for a in ("Do not spend","Not approved","Never","Abort") if d.gate_approves_spend(g(a))];print(bad);sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

import sys;sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import bl_dispatch as d;g=lambda a:{"question":"Approve spend?","options":["yes",a],"answer":a};ok=[a for a in ("Approve spend","Yes","Go ahead") if d.gate_approves_spend(g(a))];bad=[a for a in ("No","Decline","Do not spend","Don\x27t spend","Not approved","Never","Abort") if d.gate_approves_spend(g(a))];print(ok,bad);sys.exit(0 if len(ok)==3 and not bad else 1)

gates.question: How does the refusal check read an answer's leading words: the first two runs of letters anywhere in the answer, or only from its first character?
options: Letter runs: skip leading punctuation, so '- No' and '(Never)' refuse
From the first character: only an answer that starts with the word refuses
gates.recommendation: Letter runs: skip leading punctuation, so '- No' and '(Never)' refuse
gates.answer: Letter runs: skip leading punctuation, so '- No' and '(Never)' refuse
